comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh full-restart review 27 October 2026: English full-time MISOC within Public Administration; adopted ESSB 2026–2027 EER Appendix III C, printed p.39, controls the coherent 180-EC curriculum (60+60+60). The directly retrieved current public overview also lists compulsory 6.5-EC Designing Social Research; a search extraction omitted it. The adopted EER controls component and credit status. All 22 named courses are compulsory; the 15-EC minor slot requires programme-approved EUR-register choice or Examination Board exemption. Exchange/internship possibilities are conditional alternatives within that space, not extra credits. EER arts.3.3–3.6,4.1–4.3,7.4 and Appendix I MISOC outcomes govern language, progression, attendance and research. This v2 root was recovered before this restart; historical repair evidence is a lead only. Current UCR course content, names, formal prerequisites and offerings were reassessed against the authoritative enriched workbook on 31 October 2026. Public Policy Analysis is now planned and included in both alternatives; external curriculum and interest research remain retained under dependency reuse rules.

questionsApplications.label: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?
Which development and migration strategies work, and under what governance conditions?
How should climate change be governed across public, private and societal actors?
How does technological change affect public organisations?

alternatives.concept: Comparative politics, international relations and law, sociology, public policy analysis, public economics and organisational study address how public actors manage international social challenges. Qualitative and quantitative research support analysis of institutions, welfare and collective decisions.
alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines politics, international/EU law, sociology, Public Policy Analysis, public economics, organisational study and social research. It is a broad substantive response to MISOC while retaining its specialist migration/development and compulsory-project gaps.

alternatives.concept: Climate change organises public policy analysis, sustainability governance, European institutions and law, social mobilisation, public economics and organisational study. Environmental foundations, renewable-energy assessment, communication and partner research provide concrete problems and interventions for that governance study.
basisLabels: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?
How should climate change be governed across public, private and societal actors?
alternatives.labelRationale: The reconstructed 24-course programme centres climate governance and interventions, with public economics and organisational study restored. The label covers its actual social-science majority and complementary scientific/technical preparation.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Six courses differ from the broad option (45 EC): Sustainability Essentials I and II, Ethics, Communicating the Climate Crisis, Research in a Sustainable Delta and Renewable System Design. The science foundations support energy-system assessment; ethics supplies normative analysis, while climate communication and partner research change the organising problem. Public Policy Analysis is now shared core preparation, not a source of manufactured distinctness.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All 24 current planned offerings and earlier formal prerequisites verified for Fall2026–Spring2029. Year-1 PPD retained. Introductory Economics is in its sole planned Fall2026 term. Public Policy Analysis is in an actual Spring2028/2029 offering. Research Methods precedes dependent public economics and organisational study; the law gateway precedes EU/international law where selected. Sociology foundations precede later theory where feasible. The broad option retains introductory political philosophy before completion and econometrics after research-method foundations.

courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice provides a complementary legal foundation in administrative, constitutional and international law, legal systems and justice for analysing the institutions through which public decisions are made. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public administration and public policy” and “International law”.

Introduction to Sociology Classical and contemporary sociological reasoning analyses social boundaries, networks and stratification, including migration and inequalities in education and work. These concepts support analysis of the social structures underlying international challenges.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Sociology”.

Introduction to Economics Introduction to Economics provides foundational economic reasoning about incentives, welfare and resource allocation. It implements the explicit academic basis “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

Introduction to Public International Law Public international law covers treaties, legal institutions, responsibility, force and armed conflict, international crime, human rights, economic relations and environmental protection. Case exercises and a research podcast develop legal analysis of cross-border social challenges; no dedicated refugee-law syllabus is asserted.. It implements the explicit academic basis “International law” and “International social and governance challenges”.

Theory of International Relations Theory of International Relations adds international-relations theory for cross-border governance and political order. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Qualitative Research Methodology directly teaches qualitative research design, data collection, analysis and dissemination through a social research project. It implements the explicit academic basis “Qualitative and quantitative social research”.

Research Methods & Statistics Research design, measurement, sampling, surveys, experiments and statistical inference provide social-research foundations; a group project collects and analyses data using R/R Commander.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Qualitative and quantitative social research”.

Foundations of Comparative Politics Compares political institutions, parties, elections, participation and democratisation through empirical political analysis, giving specific tools for analysing government decisions and cross-national institutional differences.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

European Union Politics EU institutions, representation, interests, policymaking and implementation provide specific multi-level governance study, with empirical research on European Parliament amendments.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Introduction to Political Philosophy European and non-European political thought examines society, rights, authority and the organisation of power through original texts and normative argument, providing specific political-philosophy study.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Modern Sociology Modern and critical social theory, including Bourdieu, Black feminist and postcolonial perspectives, provides frameworks for interpreting institutions, power and unequal social outcomes.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Sociology”.

Governance of Sustainability Institutions, power, participation and justice frame collective sustainability decisions involving government, markets and civil society. Food, freshwater, energy and climate cases and a Zeeland policy-advice/evaluation project directly implement the evidenced climate-governance question.. It implements the explicit academic basis “International social and governance challenges”.
Public Economics Public Economics examines public-sector economics, taxation, welfare and resource allocation. It implements the explicit academic basis “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

Peace & Conflict Legal, sociological, political and historical approaches examine conflict, inequality, identity, international security and peacebuilding; a research dossier and policy brief apply evidence to cross-border governance problems.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Public Policy Analysis Directly studies public policymaking under globalisation through policy phases and competing conceptualisations across national and international arenas. Case analysis and policy memos implement public-policy reasoning and research-based advice.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public administration and public policy” and “Research-based advice and professional skills”.

International Macroeconomics International Macroeconomics adds macroeconomic analysis of international economic conditions and policy. It implements the explicit academic basis “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership Psychology of Organizations & Leadership provides organisational-psychology theory on motivation, leadership, groups and organisational culture. It implements the explicit academic basis “Organisation and management”.

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory Civil society, trust, social capital, public spheres, solidarity and movements provide specific frameworks for analysing nonstate actors and collective action. An empirical/documentary project does not imply mandatory NGO fieldwork.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Sociology”.

Climate Change directly examines a named MISOC challenge through climate drivers and impacts, adaptation, mitigation, justice and governance; scientific and social aspects are distinguished. It implements the explicit academic basis “International social and governance challenges”.

Foundations of European Union Law directly examines EU institutions, legal foundations, citizenship and free movement, enabling legal analysis of European governance alongside political study. It implements the explicit academic basis “Global and European governance” and “International law”.

Econometrics directly teaches quantitative causal and predictive analysis using regression, instrumental variables, statistical tests and an empirical economic paper. It implements the explicit academic basis “Qualitative and quantitative social research” and “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

Psychology of Leading Under Pressure Emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging and psychological safety examine inclusive leadership under conflict and interpersonal uncertainty. A supervised quantitative survey and empirical reports connect people-management questions to original evidence; minority experiences inform the analysis.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Organisation and management”.

Social Movements & Environmental Justice examines social movements and environmental justice using environmental-conflict cases, contributing directly to the social mobilisation and inequality dimensions of international sustainability challenges. It implements the explicit academic basis “International social and governance challenges”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two evidence-backed programmes retained after current-course review. Public Policy Analysis is now planned and directly supports the defining policy core in both options, replacing general Ethics in the broad option and additional Microeconomics in the climate option. The two programmes still differ by six substantive courses/45 EC. Reconsidered migration/development: human rights and imperial history offer complementary perspectives but do not create a distinct programme of migration policy/development strategies; unrelated swaps would manufacture the four-course floor. Reconsidered technology/public organisations: AI business, AI ethics and digital-strategy courses contribute different adjacent domains, but do not establish a sustained public-organisation technology programme. This is an academic construction limit, not an offering shortage. Stop at two.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: International law is most directly comparable to UCR Introduction to Public International Law. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.
Political Science is most directly comparable to UCR Foundations of Comparative Politics. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.
Global & European Governance is most directly comparable to UCR European Union Politics. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.

Both study political authority, rights and the justification of power. UCR surveys European and non-European thought over a longer historical span, whereas the MISOC component explicitly centres democracy. This is partial substantive correspondence, not course equivalence.

Public Policy Analysis is included in both UCR options and placed with the dedicated Policy Analysis component. The separate introductory Public Policy course remains visible rather than duplicating that UCR course.

Public Policy Analysis studies policymaking phases and alternative policy conceptualisations through a case spanning national and international arenas, with policy-memo writing. This establishes direct policy-analysis correspondence without asserting an identical methods syllabus.
Several UCR courses analyse institutions and society, but no single scheduled course establishes substantial coverage of this dedicated MISOC component.
Sociology I is most directly comparable to UCR Introduction to Sociology. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.

Organisation & Management and UCR Psychology of Organizations & Leadership both address the functioning and management of organisations. Their framing differs, but the substantive organisational domain is sufficiently shared for row alignment.

Economics, Welfare and Distribution is most directly comparable to UCR Introduction to Economics. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.

Allocation and Management of Public Resources is most directly comparable to UCR Public Economics. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.

Psychology of Leading Under Pressure directly examines emotional regulation, psychological safety and inclusive leadership in difficult social and organisational situations, with survey-based research. This supports a partial people-management relationship; it does not reproduce the full complex-organisation management syllabus.
Designing Social Research is most directly comparable to UCR Research Methods & Statistics. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.

MISOC Skills serves academic and professional skill development, while UCR Personal & Professional Development develops core academic, communication, reflection and independent-learning skills. Their educational function substantially corresponds despite different programme framing.
Qualitative Methods is most directly comparable to UCR Qualitative Research Methodology. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.
Quantitative Methods is most directly comparable to UCR Econometrics. The shared substantive domain supports comparison without implying identical content or credit weight.
A programme-approved 15-EC choice slot has no fixed academic subject to align to a scheduled UCR course.
The compulsory 15-EC MISOC project is not a scheduled UCR course. The separate optional independent research element is not included in the 180-EC UCR total.

Network Governance and UCR Governance of Sustainability both center governance as multi-actor collective decision-making involving public and non-public actors around public problems. UCR applies the governance framework to sustainability, but the primary governance content substantially corresponds.

Both are dedicated project-based research courses. UCR Research in a Sustainable Delta has students conduct an externally grounded research project in teams; the sustainability theme changes the application domain, not the central research-project educational function.
The broad introductory MISOC challenge course is not reducible to UCR Climate Change or Peace & Conflict; it remains separately visible.
The UCR programmes include relevant global, economic and social perspectives, without a dedicated development-issues course.
International law, EU free movement and sociology provide partial perspectives, without the dedicated migration-policy course.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme combines a structured Public Administration curriculum with international law, migration, development, research methods and a bachelor project. UCR can assemble strong multidisciplinary programmes around global governance and specific international challenges, but does not reproduce the same dedicated MISOC sequence or its named International Migration and Global Development Issues courses.

audience.programmeDescription: Management of International Social Challenges at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines how public organisations address problems across national borders, including migration, global development, climate change and economic instability. Students study politics, policy, international law, sociology, economics and management alongside social research and a bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR options include Public Policy Analysis alongside politics, sociology, public economics, organisations and social research. The broad option adds international law, political philosophy and quantitative economic methods; the climate option adds environmental foundations, energy-system assessment, communication and partner research. Neither reproduces Erasmus’s dedicated migration/development courses, full public-administration sequence or required 15-EC bachelor project.
